record.paper_title: Realistic shell-model calculations: current status and open problems
record.context_brief: Validity of omitting U and bubble diagrams
record.original_question: When the auxiliary one-body potential U in realistic shell-model calculations is taken to be a harmonic-oscillator potential rather than a Hartree-Fock self-consistent potential, is it justified to omit diagrams containing U and bubble insertions on the assumption that they cancel, or do those omitted terms make a significant contribution to the effective interaction?

evidence.quote: However, in almost all calculations performed so far diagrams with the U potential and bubble insertions are not included. This assumption is based on the fact that these diagrams would cancel each other when using for U the Hartree-Fock self-consistent potential.
The most common choice, however, is the harmonic oscillator potential, and the plausibility of the above approximation remains to be ascertained.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the linked-cluster perturbation expansion of the shell-model effective interaction $V_{\rm eff}$, one starts from a nuclear Hamiltonian
$$H = T + V_{NN} = (T+U) + (V_{NN}-U) \equiv H_0 + H_1,$$
where $T$ is the kinetic energy, $V_{NN}$ is the realistic nucleon–nucleon interaction, and $U$ is an auxiliary one-body potential introduced so that $H_0$ provides a convenient single-particle basis. The Goldstone (folded-diagram) expansion of $V_{\rm eff}$ then contains, in addition to diagrams built only from the residual two-body interaction $V_{NN}-U$ (often re-summed into the $G$-matrix or $V_{\rm low\,k}$), a class of diagrams featuring insertions of the one-body operator $-U$ on internal lines together with the so-called "bubble" (Hartree–Fock-like) self-energy insertions generated by $V_{NN}$.

If $U$ is chosen self-consistently as the Hartree–Fock potential of the occupied orbitals, then to a given order the $-U$ insertions exactly cancel the bubble self-energy insertions, and both classes of diagrams may be omitted from $V_{\rm eff}$ without loss.

Suppose instead that $U$ is taken to be a harmonic-oscillator potential, $U(r) = \tfrac{1}{2} m\omega^2 r^2$, which is not self-consistent with respect to $V_{NN}$. The question is the following:

Is the omission of all diagrams in the perturbative expansion of $V_{\rm eff}$ that contain $-U$ insertions and/or bubble self-energy insertions still justified in this case, or do these omitted diagrams contribute non-negligibly (i.e., comparable in size to other terms retained at the same order) to the matrix elements of $V_{\rm eff}$ in realistic shell-model calculations? Provide a quantitative criterion under which the cancellation can be regarded as approximately valid for a harmonic-oscillator choice of $U$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a definitive quantitative study establishing whether the cancellation between U-insertion and bubble (self-energy) diagrams remains valid when U is taken to be the harmonic-oscillator potential rather than the Hartree–Fock self-consistent potential. The question is generally regarded as an open methodological issue in realistic shell-model perturbation theory; standard treatments simply omit these diagrams as a working assumption.

status_evidence.title: Form of the effective interaction in harmonic-oscillator-based effective theory
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses construction of effective interactions in a harmonic-oscillator basis but does not resolve the cancellation question for U and bubble insertions.
status_evidence.claim: Available HO-basis effective-interaction studies do not provide a definitive resolution of the U / bubble cancellation issue.

status_evidence.title: Effective field theory in the harmonic oscillator basis
status_evidence.snippet: Develops EFT in HO basis; treats single-particle potential choices but without quantitative bound on omitted U/bubble diagrams.
status_evidence.claim: No quantitative justification of omitting U-insertion and bubble diagrams for HO U is established.
